yara: Pushing up results from the gull-int8 onboarding wave. We
re seeing a low-rate class of structured-output failures in the funcall suite: people hitting 'root not object' or 'schema missing: actions'. Failure mode looks different hererom usual: some payloads arrive with duplicated trailing brackets `...]}]` and others have an extra leading comma before the first element. Rate ~7/1000 under segmented streaming + kvcache prefix.

vijay: Can you attach a couple of sanitized raw captures? Duplicated brackets might indicate a chunk-splice duplication on reassembly rather than pure truncation.

yara: Pasting two sanitized examples from captures (IDs redacted):

```json
// example 1 - duplicate close bracket
{"actions": [{"tool":"create_issue","params":{"title":"deploy"}}]}]

// example 2 - leading comma then array
, [ {"tool":"ping","params":{"target":"infra"}} ]
```

megan: Interesting. Baseline fp16 run has effectively zero. Correlation: segmented stream mode with chunk size 128 + prefix kvcache enabled + batch >= 6. Also we see a higher incidence when kernel hint is 'packed-fast' on sequences > 420.

sys-bot: canary started 2026-08-02T12:00:00Z: job cj-3221 model=gull-int8 nodes=2 batch=8 mode=segmented. Artifacts (token_stream + chunk_map): https://ci.internal/canary/cj-3221 :satellite:

vijay: Hypotheses: (A) reassembly logic duplicates the last chunk when a cached prefix is spliced in, producing an extra close bracket, (B) token-level tokenization under int8 can emit a free-standing comma token in some kernel paths, or (C) client-side streaming buffer glue does an extra flush that leaves a leading comma. We should correlate chunk_map offsets with the duplicated bytes in token_stream.

yara: I ran quick ablations: segmented=off (continuous stream) => 0.9/1000; segmented=on + kvcache=off => 1.1/1000; segmented=on + kvcache=on => 7.2/1000. Anchoring the prompt with explicit terminator "<ACTIONS_END>" reduced to 0.3/1000. So strong interaction between segmented assembly and cached prefix.

megan: Good repro signal. Immediate mitigation options: 1) patch reassembler to dedupe adjacent chunk boundaries (if last byte of previous chunk == first byte of next chunk and both are JSON terminators/commas, collapse), 2) runtime sentinel injection on retriever, 3) postprocess normalizer that safely canonicalizes top-level arrays and removes stray leading commas before parse (counts as a retryable event).

vijay: For safety I'm going to push a short-lived postprocess normalizer in the function runner that does two things: strip leading commas/tokens before trying JSON.parse, and if parse still fails attempt a wrap into {"actions": <payload>} and mark the metric as "heuristic_wrap". Keep retry budget shallow (max 1 retry) to avoid latency blowups.

yara: Also request infra to attach chunk_map + kernel selection per request for failing traces so we can see whether duplicated bytes align with cached-chunk pivots. If the reassembler is at fault we'll land a small fix to recompute chunk offsets after prefix splicing.

canary-bot: replay job 2026-08-02T12:35:00Z finished: seeds=4000 metrics: segmented+kvcache ON => 6.9/1000 parse_fail; segmented ON kvcache OFF => 1.0/1000; segmented OFF kvcache ON => 0.8/1000. Collected artifacts at https://ci.internal/canary/cj-3221/artifacts :mag:

megan: OK looks decisive. Plan: 1) keep kvcache disabled for segmented streaming on production-int8 for the moment, 2) merge postprocess normalizer as emergency patch with metric tags and alert on >1/1000 heuristic_wrap, 3) land reassembler dedupe fix and run a seeded replay to validate.

vijay: I'll open the infra ticket linking chunk_map + token_stream and add a tiny unit test for chunk reassembly that exercises a cached-prefix splice. If reassembler fix passes unit + canary replay we can re-enable kvcache for segmented flows.

yara: Thanks. If anyone finds a non-retryable garbage payload paste raw token hex here. Also shout if we want to run a mirror fallback (fp16) for user-facing routes while canary is in flight. :pray:
